title: What can you say about rhodiola in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for rhodiola; the strongest is "Used in herbal medicine to help temporarily relieve symptoms of stress, such as mental fatigue and a feeling of weakness" (moderate, 144-680 mg standardized extract a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats depression or anxiety".

supported_wordings.wording: Used in herbal medicine to help temporarily relieve symptoms of stress, such as mental fatigue and a feeling of weakness.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it as a herbal medicine use at 144-680 mg of standardized extract a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; at most 200 mg per dose; extract standardized to 0.8-3% salidroside and/or 1-6% rosavins. Health Canada also accepts a non-standardized ethanolic dry extract (144-400 mg a day, equal to 216-2,000 mg dried root) and a tincture (1.2-1.8 g dried root a day). Avoid taking it before bedtime.
supported_wordings.form: Standardized dry extract of root or root and rhizome

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.
